common.settingsScreenshotAlt: The settings window with the Essentials group expanded and General settings below

noReleases.message: There are no releases yet. You can build Flotilla from source or subscribe to release notifications on GitHub.
noReleases.watchHint: To hear about new versions, choose Watch › Custom › Releases on GitHub.

common.firstLaunchBlocked: Flotilla hasn’t been notarized by Apple, so macOS blocks it the first time you try to open it. The alert says Apple cannot verify that it is free of malware.

accessibility.settingsPath: You can enable it in System Settings › Privacy & Security › Accessibility. On macOS 27, go to Privacy & Security › Device Control and Data Access.
accessibility.reenable: Because Flotilla uses ad-hoc signing, you may need to enable this permission again after an update.

withoutAccessibility.nearPointer: The panel appears near the pointer and may not line up exactly with the group icon
withoutAccessibility.slower: The panel takes a little longer to open after a click

common.buildRequirements: Building Flotilla requires the Xcode Command Line Tools and mise. You don’t need the full Xcode app.

meta.title: Flotilla — Keep your Dock organized.
meta.description: Group apps, files, folders, and web pages in your Mac’s Dock.

hero.title: Keep your Dock organized.
hero.lead: Group apps, files, folders, and web pages in your Mac’s Dock.
hero.screenshotAlt: The Essentials group open above the Dock, showing apps and a folder in a grid, with an arrow pointing to the group icon

statement: The Dock’s own folders sit on the right.
Flotilla lets you group your apps on the left.

groups.title: Flotilla’s groups
groups.position: In the app section, on the left

highlights.noFolders: Grouping doesn’t move your apps or files, and you don’t need to create any folders on disk.
highlights.mixedItems: Apps, files, Finder folders, and web pages can all share the same group.
highlights.nativeGrid: Click a group icon to open a grid with the same look and animations as the Dock’s built-in folders.

features.title: Organize apps, files, and web pages.

folders.title: Browse folders in the panel
folders.description: Folders open in the same panel, with file thumbnails. To switch to Finder, choose Open in Finder at the end of the grid.
folders.backButton: Use the back button to go up one level
folders.hiddenFiles: Turn on Show hidden files in settings
folders.screenshotAlt: The Wallpapers folder open in the panel, showing image thumbnails and Open in Finder at the end

dragAndDrop.title: Drag and drop
dragAndDrop.description: Drop apps, files, or folders onto a group icon in the Dock or a group in the settings window. You can drop web pages into the settings window too.

settings.title: Manage groups in the settings window
settings.add: Click Add… to choose apps, files, folders, or web pages
settings.rename: Double-click a group to rename it
settings.reorder: Drag items in the list to reorder them or move them into another group
settings.moreOptions: Right-click or Control-click an item for more options

alongsideApps.title: Groups alongside your apps
alongsideApps.description: Each top-level group appears on the left side of the Dock with its own name and icon.

mixedItems.title: Apps, files, and web pages
mixedItems.description: Keep apps, files, folders, and web pages together. Files open in their default app, and web pages open in your default browser.

nestedGroups.title: Groups within groups
nestedGroups.description: You can add groups inside other groups. Open a subgroup to browse it, then use the back button to return.

gridView.title: Grid view
gridView.description: Groups open in a grid above the Dock, aligned with their icons.

iconPreviews.title: Group icon previews
iconPreviews.description: The group icon previews the first few items, up to four. You can adjust the number in settings. Its background follows your Mac’s light or dark appearance.

reorderAndRemove.title: Reorder and remove
reorderAndRemove.description: Drag items in the panel to reorder them. To remove one, drag it outside, wait for Remove to appear, then let go.

tracking.title: Keeps track of your items
tracking.description: Apps and files still open from a group after you move or rename them. After an app update, Flotilla opens the newly installed version.

background.title: Runs in the background
background.description: Flotilla runs in the menu bar and stays out of the Dock, even when a panel is open. Panels don’t take focus away from your current app.

languages.title: Five languages
languages.description: English, Simplified Chinese, Traditional Chinese, Japanese, and Korean. The app uses your system language, or English if that language isn’t supported.

howItWorks.title: How does a group get into the Dock?
howItWorks.lead: To give a group a place in the Dock’s app section, Flotilla creates a placeholder app for each top-level group and adds it with the group’s name and icon.

click.title: Click a group icon
click.description: The Dock launches the placeholder app for that group.

openURL.title: The placeholder opens a flotilla:// URL
openURL.description: It uses this URL to notify Flotilla, then quits without bringing another app to the front.

panel.title: Flotilla opens or closes the panel
panel.description: If Flotilla isn’t running, macOS launches it first. The placeholder also forwards items dropped onto the group icon to Flotilla.

changes.title: What does Flotilla change on your Mac?

dockIcons.title: Only Flotilla’s group icons
dockIcons.preferences: Flotilla manages group icons through the Dock preferences (com.apple.dock).
dockIcons.scope: It changes only its own entries in persistent-apps, the group icons on the left side of the Dock. Other icons and Dock settings stay as they are.

dockRestart.title: The Dock restarts after each change
dockRestart.description: After a change to the Dock preferences, Flotilla ends the Dock process. macOS automatically restarts it so the change can take effect.

backup.title: Backed up before changes
backup.description: Each time Flotilla launches, it exports a full backup of com.apple.dock before making its first change. It keeps the five most recent backups.

data.title: Data and settings
data.dockTiles: DockTiles/: the placeholder apps for top-level groups
data.settings: Settings are stored in the preferences domain com.rakuyo.flotilla.

network.title: Network access
network.description: Flotilla connects to the internet to fetch page titles and to check for and download updates from GitHub Releases. Automatic checks can be turned off in Software Update settings.

openSource.title: Code and discussions on GitHub.
openSource.lead: Flotilla is free and open source. You can browse the code, report a problem, or help with development on GitHub.

follow.title: Follow the project
follow.description: If you like Flotilla, give it a star on GitHub. To hear about new versions, choose Watch › Custom › Releases.

issues.title: Report a problem
issues.description: Something not working? You can report it in GitHub Issues.

contribute.title: Contribute
contribute.description: Before opening a pull request, run mise run swift:lint and swift test and make sure both pass.

license.description: Flotilla is licensed under the GNU General Public License v3.0.

blocked.question: Why does macOS block Flotilla the first time I open it?
blocked.openAnyway: Click Done, then open System Settings › Privacy & Security and click Open Anyway under Security. The button is available for an hour after you try to open Flotilla.

withoutAccessibility.question: Can I use Flotilla without Accessibility access?

reenable.question: Why might I need to enable Accessibility again after an update?

dockRestart.question: Why does the Dock restart?
dockRestart.reason: Flotilla changes the Dock preferences to add or update group icons. It then ends the Dock process, and macOS automatically restarts it so the change can take effect.
dockRestart.triggers: Group previews and switches between light and dark appearance also update the icons, so they trigger a Dock restart too.

removeIcon.question: How do I remove a group icon from the Dock and add it back?
removeIcon.remove: Drag the group icon out of the Dock to remove it.
removeIcon.addBack: The group stays in the settings window, marked Not in Dock, and won’t return to the Dock automatically. To bring the icon back, right-click the group and choose Add to Dock.

requirements.question: Which Macs does Flotilla run on?
requirements.answer: Flotilla runs on Macs with Apple silicon and macOS 15 or later.

languages.question: Which languages does Flotilla support?
languages.answer: English, Simplified Chinese, Traditional Chinese, Japanese, and Korean. The app uses your system language, or English if that language isn’t supported.
languages.appName: The app’s name follows your system language too: 归帆 in Simplified Chinese, 歸帆 in Traditional Chinese, 帰帆 in Japanese, and Flotilla in other languages.

steps.unzip: Unzip the download and drag Flotilla.app into Applications

meta.title: Download Flotilla
meta.description: Download Flotilla to group apps in your Dock. For Macs with Apple silicon and macOS 15 or later, with help for installation, first launch, and permissions.

card.label: Download

fallback.title: The latest version
fallback.description: Download the latest Flotilla-X.Y.Z.zip from the Releases page on GitHub.

card.nextSteps: Next, follow the installation steps below

install.title: Install Flotilla and get it set up.

unzip.title: Unzip and move to Applications
unzip.description: Double-click the downloaded Flotilla-X.Y.Z.zip to unzip it, then drag Flotilla.app into the Applications folder.
unzip.note: Finder uses the app’s name in your system language, such as 归帆 in Simplified Chinese.

firstLaunch.title: Open it for the first time
firstLaunch.dismiss: Click Done to dismiss the alert, then follow these steps to open Flotilla:
firstLaunch.openAnyway: Scroll down to Security, find the message about Flotilla being blocked, and click Open Anyway
firstLaunch.openAnywayNote: This button only appears for an hour after you try to open Flotilla
firstLaunch.password: Confirm with your login password when prompted
firstLaunch.done: You can now open Flotilla normally.
firstLaunch.terminal: If you prefer Terminal, run this command to remove the quarantine attribute, then open Flotilla:

why.question: Why does macOS block Flotilla?
why.answer: Flotilla uses ad-hoc signing and hasn’t been notarized by Apple. This triggers a macOS security alert on first launch.
appleGuide: For more about these checks and how to allow an app to open, see Apple’s guide,

accessibility.title: Enable Accessibility access
accessibility.purpose: Accessibility access lets Flotilla read the Dock’s interface so it can:
accessibility.locate: Locate the group icon so the panel can line up with it
accessibility.openOnRelease: Open the panel as soon as you release the mouse button, just like a Dock folder
accessibility.prompt: If access hasn’t been granted, macOS prompts you the first time you click a group icon after each launch of Flotilla.

reenable.title: You may need to enable it again

files.title: Files and folders
files.description: The first time you open a folder in Documents, Desktop, Downloads, or another protected location through Flotilla, macOS asks for access. Flotilla needs your permission to read and display the folder’s contents.

copyButton.copied: Copied — paste it into Terminal to run
copyButton.label: Copy

getStarted.title: Create your first group.
getStarted.lead: Click the sailing ship in the menu bar and choose Settings… to manage your groups. Quit Flotilla is in the same menu.

create.title: Create a group
create.newGroup: Under Groups, click New Group, type a name, and press Return
create.newGroupNote: The Dock briefly restarts, then shows the group icon in the app section on the left
create.add: Select the group, click Add…, and choose Add Apps…, Add Files…, or Add Web Page…
create.drop: You can also drop apps, files, or folders onto a group in the settings window or its Dock icon. For web pages, drag them from your browser into a group in the settings window

panel.title: Use the panel
panel.open: Click a group icon in the Dock, then select the app, file, or web page you want to open
panel.browse: Click a subgroup or folder to open it. Use the back button to go up one level
panel.close: Click the group icon again, click outside the panel, or press Esc to close it
panel.reorder: Drag items within a group to change their order
panel.remove: To remove an item, drag it out of the panel, wait for Remove to appear, and let go

getStarted.readme: The full guide is in the README

build.title: Build instructions

commandLineTools.title: Xcode Command Line Tools 26 or later
commandLineTools.description: Version 26 includes Swift 6.2 and the macOS 26 SDK. The panel uses NSGlassEffectView, so this SDK is needed to build it.

mise.description: Runs the build commands defined in mise.toml.

commands.bundleComment: Build the release version, bundle it as build/Flotilla.app, and ad-hoc sign it

notes.ldWarning: You can ignore the two ld: warning: search path ... not found warnings during the build. They refer to directories that aren’t included in the Command Line Tools.
notes.quitInstalled: Quit the installed copy of Flotilla before launching build/Flotilla.app. If a copy is already running, launching another only activates the existing one.

build.readme: Tests, code style, and more in the README

meta.description: Browse Flotilla’s release notes, release dates, and download links.

hero.title: Release notes
hero.lead: Find out what changed in each release and download the version you need.

fallback.title: Release notes are on GitHub
fallback.description: Visit GitHub Releases to read the notes for each version and download a copy.
